verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's own docs describe running the core product (MongoDB, API and front-end) on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose. That is corroborated by a community report of production self-hosted use and by a hands-on probe that booted the official image and completed a flag create-and-evaluate loop with no account or license. Community requests for a non-Docker install and complaints about the MongoDB dependency are limitations, not contradictions. Missing for 10: a documented non-Docker install path, and evidence on whether paid-tier features are available when self-hosted.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Run GrowthBook on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose, including MongoDB, the API, and the front-end.
Then, just run `docker compose up -d` to start everything and view the app at http://localhost:3000
We have used the self-hosted version a few months in my company now, and are very happy about it.
